text:
ashley: Quick idea — add a 'fast preview' card into the Cost Console that shows per-route token burn + estimated cache savings + top model SKUs. One-glance triage for routing/quota/regression issues. Thoughts?

ryan: +1. Love the quick insight. Question: is this purely UI or do we need new backend telemetry/estimator? How do we compute cache savings reliably — sampled hits or lineage extrapolation?

sophia: We should add a bounded estimator. Proposal: sample the last 1h of requests with a KV-hit flag and extrapolate. Add a tiny telemetry event `cache_hit_sampled` with {route_gv, model_sku, seq_len, hit}. Keep payload minimal.

kevin: New events increase ingestion. Can we piggyback on existing batcher metrics instead of emitting a new event type? Also we need stable mapping for route vs alias — console needs consistent grouping.

ashley: Piggybacking is ok if we include a low-cardinality shim: `route_gv` (grouped route) + `hotpath_bucket`. That keeps cardinality down.

jules: UX Q: should this be an inline per-route row summary or a top-level flyout? Ops wants glanceable rows; PMs want CSV export.

ryan: I prefer row inline with a hover for details. Also we should add a 'what-if' toggle: estimate delta if we flip on aggressive batching or quantization. Quick decision tool for routing changes.

sophia: For the 'what-if' calc we need model cost profiles. We can reuse the existing `model_sku_profile` (per-token-cost, latency) and apply a simple multiplier for quantization/batching effects.

kevin: Security concern: surfacing estimated absolute dollars for tenants might leak pricing. Guardrail: show relative % savings to non-admins and full numbers only to org owners.

ashley: Agreed. We'll show percents + anonymized low/medium/high labels for most users. Admins/owners get the absolute numbers. Flagging: `cost_console_fastpreview_v1`.

ops-bot: feature-flag created: cost_console_fastpreview_v1 — enabled in dev, disabled in prod.

ryan: Rollout plan suggestion: canary to 5% of orgs for 48h, gather telemetry + manual feedback. Telemetry events to add: `fastpreview_render` (route_id, user_tier) and `fastpreview_feedback` (opt-in comment). Do we backfill historical estimates?

sophia: Backfilling is expensive. Let's compute hourly forward-only. Store estimates for 6h TTL. Keep `sample_count` and confidence label to communicate noise.

kevin: API/infra notes: expose internal API GET /internal/cost-fastpreview?route_id=... that returns a compact shape: percent_savings, raw_estimate, sample_count, top_model_skus. Secure it to console service account + rate limit.

ashley: Action items: 1) ryan + kevin scope API + rate limits, 2) sophia implements estimator + telemetry, 3) jules designs inline row card & CSV export, 4) ash coordinates rollout flag and permisssions. I'll open a tracking issue and PR.

ryan: I'll open the PR for API shape + canary config. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/9876

sophia: Note: low-volume routes will be noisy. We must expose `sample_count` & a confidence band: low/medium/high. Also add a small explainer tooltip: "estimates use sampled KV-hit telemetry and extrapolate — noisy for <50 samples".

jules: Love the tooltip. Sync tomorrow 10am to finalize microcopy and export columns. Anyone blocked?

kevin: Need clarification on `route_gv` mapping from infra owners. I'll ping infra and follow up.

ashley: Thanks all :thumbsup: — opening tracking issue now and will assign owners.
